title: nfl-urls
universal_lens: A unified mathematical framework for NFL player performance metrics integrating alignment, coverage, and efficiency through stochastic process modeling. The chapter window delineates a high-dimensional state-space where offensive and defensive actions are mapped to expected point advantages (EPA) and spatial dominance. The primitives form a tensor product of coverage schemes, alignment vectors, and red-zone constraints, unifying discrete play-calling probabilities with continuous spatial yield metrics.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference on player-specific stochastic processes using conformal predictive distributions over alignment and coverage data for probabilistic forecasting. GSI employs Bayesian hierarchical modeling over the provided URL endpoints to infer latent player talent and team schematic tendencies. Conformal prediction intervals are constructed around EPA-per-play and unrealized air yards, quantifying epistemic uncertainty in target-share distributions and pressure-rate-over-expected metrics across varying game scripts.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning engine maps real-time player states into transition matrices of alignment and coverage regimes for dynamic tactical adaptation. GSE translates these primitives into a Markov Decision Process for situational reasoning. State transitions are driven by pace-playcalling rates and trench-play success, while the reward function is dynamically optimized using win-yards and fantasy-points-per-route-allowed, enabling real-time exploitation of defensive coverage vulnerabilities.

primitives.name: In-Line Tight End Percentage
primitives.assumptions: Player alignment is quantized into discrete positional categories; in-line TE usage is independent of opponent defensive scheme.
primitives.breakdown_regime: P_{\text{in-line TE}} \to 0 when TE is not aligned in-line.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's player positioning kernel, where P_{\text{in-line TE}} maps to a conditional probability distribution over tight end alignment configurations.
layer2.telemetry: Observed percentage of snaps with TE in-line position.

primitives.name: Average Depth of Target Allowed
primitives.assumptions: Target depth is measured relative to line of scrimmage; average is computed across all allowed targets.

layer2.mapping: Derived from GSE's coverage kernel, representing expected target depth under defensive pressure.
layer2.telemetry: Mean yards beyond line of scrimmage for allowed passes.

primitives.name: Fantasy Points Per Target Allowed
primitives.assumptions: Fantasy scoring is linearly additive across receiver types; target count is normalized by game time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: F_{\text{pt/target}} \to 0 when no targets are allowed.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's fantasy scoring kernel via direct correspondence between allowed targets and scoring outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Average fantasy points scored per allowed pass target.

primitives.name: Scramble Rate When Pressured
primitives.assumptions: Pressured situations are defined as snaps with defensive pressure applied; scrambling is binary outcome.

layer2.mapping: Derived from GSE's quarterback decision-making kernel, modeling reactive behavior under pressure.
layer2.telemetry: Fraction of pressured snaps resulting in scrambles.

primitives.name: Unrealized Air Yards Operator
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: UAY: Unrealized Air Yards (yards), N: number of drops (dimensionless), Y_caught: downfield location of catch (yards), Y_thrown: downfield location of release (yards).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes perfect tracking data for ball release and receiver position; isolates receiver error from quarterback placement.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singular when tracking data fails or on intentional incomplete passes thrown behind the line of scrimmage.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSI's drop probability kernel, penalizing receivers who fail to convert positive expected value throws.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical observable via Next Gen Stats tracking coordinates.

primitives.name: Red Zone Spatial Compression Metric
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P(TD): Probability of touchdown (dimensionless), A(x): Available passing area at yardline x (sq yards), d_def: Defensive depth (yards), sigma: Variance parameter (yards).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes defensive stacking increases exponentially as field area decreases; isolates positional efficiency within constrained geometries.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if play-action artificially expands effective field area or during obvious run plays.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's constrained optimization module, evaluating talent density under boundary conditions.
layer2.telemetry: Verified via inside-10 and inside-5 reception rates per route run.

primitives.name: Coverage Explosive Suppression Kernel
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: R_exp: Explosive reception rate allowed (dimensionless), M: total receptions, Y_thresh: explosive threshold (e.g., 20 yards), N_routes: routes run, alpha_cov: coverage scheme adjustment factor.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a fixed yardage threshold defines 'explosive'; accounts for man vs zone coverage variance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when sample size of deep attempts approaches zero, rendering the rate statistically unstable.

layer2.mapping: Feeds directly into GSI's defensive secondary valuation model, adjusting for scheme difficulty.
layer2.telemetry: Measured via explosive-reception-rate-allowed and average-cushion-allowed endpoints.

primitives.name: Trench Play Pressure Differential
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: PRoE: Pressure Rate Over Expected (dimensionless), PR_obs: Observed pressure rate, PR_exp: Expected pressure rate based on base defense and QB pocket time.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a robust baseline model for expected pressure exists independent of pass rusher talent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when non-standard defensive packages (e.g., extreme exotic blitzes) violate the baseline scheme assumptions.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's offensive line protection matrix, dictating state transitions for hurried throws.
layer2.telemetry: Validated against defensive-pressure-rate-over-expected and yards-before-contact metrics.

primitives.name: Target Rate Allowed Under Coverage
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{t,c}': 'Target rate allowed per coverage type c, measured in targets per hour'}
primitives.assumptions: Receiver performance is conditionally independent of defensive scheme given target exposure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Coverage types 0–9 represent increasing complexity of man-to-zone switching.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's target allocation kernel via conditional expectation of target rate under coverage.
layer2.telemetry: Observed target rate variance across coverage types.

primitives.name: Yards Per Route Run Allowed
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Y_{r,c}': 'Average yards gained per route run under coverage c, measured in yards'}
primitives.assumptions: Route execution efficiency varies inversely with defensive pressure intensity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Coverage regimes 0–9 indicate increasing defensive tightness.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's route execution kernel via expected gain per route under coverage.

primitives.name: Reception Yield Per Coverage
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Y_{r,c}': 'Total receiving yards per reception under coverage c, measured in yards'}
primitives.assumptions: Yield is a function of both target quality and coverage density.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Coverage types 0–9 reflect increasing defensive engagement.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's yield estimation kernel via weighted average of yardage per reception.
layer2.telemetry: Observed cumulative receiving yardage under coverage types.

primitives.name: Target Separation Under Coverage
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_{c}': 'Average separation between target and defender under coverage c, measured in feet'}
primitives.assumptions: Separation increases with defensive aggressiveness and decreases with receiver speed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Coverage types 0–9 denote increasing defender proximity.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's spatial awareness kernel via separation distance metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Defensive spacing variance under different coverage types.

primitives.name: Rushing Efficiency Index
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'y_i': 'yards gained in rush i (yd)', 'a_i': 'rush attempts in play i (dimensionless)', 'n': 'total number of rushes (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear scaling of yardage per attempt; independence of individual rushes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( \sum a_i < 1 \) or \( y_i \to 0 \), REI approaches zero.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's offensive state transition probabilities via dynamic programming optimization.
layer2.telemetry: Average yards per rush attempt over time series.

primitives.name: Quarterly Scoring Distribution
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_k': 'score in quarter k (points)', 'K': 'number of quarters (dimensionless)', 'Q_k': 'quarter k (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Scoring events are independent across quarters.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's temporal scoring model under Poisson process assumption.

primitives.name: Passing Defense Pressure Rate
primitives.assumptions: Pressure rate is proportional to pass attempt frequency and sack likelihood.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( A \to 0 \), \( \rho_p \to 0 \); when \( σ_s \to 1 \), maximum pressure impact.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to compute defensive pressure influence on quarterback decision-making.
layer2.telemetry: Game-level pressure-to-attempt ratio adjusted for sacks.

primitives.name: Special Teams Field Goal Block Ratio
primitives.assumptions: Block events are independent and uniformly distributed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( A_{fg} \to 0 \), \( \beta_{fg} \to 0 \); when \( B_{fg} \to A_{fg} \), maximum blocking efficiency.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's special teams risk assessment via binary classification models.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of field goal attempts blocked per game.

reasoning_traces.think: The mathematical architecture presented in pages 5 through 8 constructs a rigorous framework for decomposing American football into orthogonal performance vectors. We begin with the individual receiver's contribution, isolated via the Unrealized Air Yards operator, which cleanly separates quarterback throw quality from receiver hands and route-running precision. This metric acts as a foundational scalar field over the spatial domain of the field. Moving outward, the Red Zone Spatial Compression primitive introduces boundary conditions, demonstrating how talent evaluation must be normalized against the shrinking geometric volume available for play execution. The transition from individual to collective dynamics is captured by the Coverage Explosive Suppression Kernel, which models the defensive secondary's ability to truncate the tail of the passing distribution. Finally, the Trench Play Pressure Differential anchors these aerial metrics to the ground game, establishing that all passing efficiency is ultimately conditional on the binary outcome of the initial engagement along the line of scrimmage. Together, these primitives form a cohesive state-transition system where EPA is the ultimate currency, derived from the interplay of spatial control, timing accuracy, and physical dominance. Each primitive encodes a functional relationship between coverage type and receiver outcome, enabling state transition modeling in situational reasoning engines.
